title: Ghormeh Sabzi
subtitle: Persian herb and lamb stew with kidney beans
excerpt: An Iranian lamb stew built on a huge quantity of slowly cooked fresh herbs, kidney beans, and lemon. The herbs are the main ingredient here, not a garnish; they cook down over 90 minutes into something dark, concentrated, and deeply flavoured. Serve with steamed basmati rice.
sourceNotes: Based on the Persian ghormeh sabzi, considered one of Iran's national dishes. The herb mixture traditionally includes dried fenugreek; this version uses a generous ratio of parsley and coriander as the base.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well and improves with time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew tastes better the next day. Make it up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently.

content.text: The herbs must be fried in oil before the liquid is added. This step develops the dark colour and concentrated flavour that defines ghormeh sabzi. Do not rush it; give the herbs at least 15 minutes in the oil.

items.prepNote: roughly chopped, included with the herb mixture

content.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large stockpot over a medium-high heat. Brown the lamb chunks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch until coloured on most sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the turmeric and cumin and cook for 1 minute.

Push the onion to one side. Add the remaining tablespoon of oil and the chopped herbs and spring onion. Fry the herbs over a medium heat, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes until very dark and fragrant.
Return the lamb to the pot. Add the chicken stock, lemon juice, and kidney beans. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 70 to 80 minutes until the lamb is very tender. Stir every 20 minutes and add a splash of water if the stew looks dry.
Season with salt and more lemon juice to taste. Serve with steamed basmati rice.

items.cause: Too much lemon added at the start
items.fix: Add lemon in stages at the end only; taste as you go.

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after 80 minutes
items.cause: Pieces were too large or heat too low
items.fix: Cover and cook for another 30 minutes over low heat.

items.symptom: Herbs are still bright green, not dark
items.cause: Not fried long enough in oil
items.fix: Fry herbs for at least 15 minutes until very dark before adding liquid.
